correctness.rationale: For rank-one residual, exact trial-plane isometry gives H=K+gr^T. Its discriminant is Δ²+(g^Tr)²−2Δ(g1r1−g2r2). Sign reduction restricts a negative discriminant to one angular quadrant; balanced r reduces it to 1+t²sin²ψ−2t cosψ, with explicit root h(t), probability arccos(h)/π and unique t=√2 maximum 1/4. A positive-definite 3×3 Aδ has Ritz gap δ and balanced residual; sketch Gram eigenvalues 1±√2δ and 1 yield exact probability 1/4 as distortion tends to zero. The checker recomputes identities and tests exact rational matrices, while finite sampling is explicitly supplemental, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Real-valued sketched eigensolvers must accommodate complex 2×2 Ritz outputs. An exact one-quarter risk under a natural rotationally symmetric residual coupling, together with an attainable all-distortion-to-zero SPD family and a sharp gap/residual transition, establishes a motivated numerical stability benchmark beyond a trivial example. It quantitatively demonstrates that small embedding distortion alone, without controlling the Ritz gap relative to residual coupling, does not uniformly prevent complex Ritz pairs.
